advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Handle committed foreign paths distinctly (commit the removal via the sanctioned push path, or report that committed pollution requires a further step) rather than reporting 'repaired'.
evidence: fsck distinguishes committed foreign paths as 'strictly worse than a working-tree stray' — src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:456-461 ('are COMMITTED to the tickets branch … and will propagate on the next push')
No commit/push of the staged deletion occurs in tracker_maintenance.py before the 'repaired' message at line 271-273.
advisory.finding: For a foreign top-level path that is COMMITTED to the tickets branch, --clean runs `git rm -r --cached` plus a filesystem delete but never commits the removal, and reports 'repaired' with exit 0. The pollution therefore still exists on origin/tickets and can be re-materialized on the next fetch/reset reconverge, so the operator is told the store is repaired when the committed pollution persists.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Single-source the tracker-maintenance help text (render help/tracker-maintenance.txt from _parse rather than a duplicated _USAGE literal).
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/help/tracker-maintenance.txt:1-21: fuller text with Safety envelope + exit codes
src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:648-649 routes `<sub> --help` (first arg) to _emit_subcommand_help(sub); _parse at tracker_maintenance.py:177-179 handles --help anywhere else via _USAGE
advisory.finding: The in-process _USAGE string duplicates the opening of help/tracker-maintenance.txt but omits the safety-envelope/exit-code sections, and _parse prints _USAGE for a `--help` that appears anywhere except first-arg position (which is intercepted to render the .txt). The two help texts can drift and give inconsistent help depending on argument position.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that creates an unmerged/conflicted index entry in the tracker and asserts `--clean` clears it (regenerable restored from HEAD, stranded-foreign removed), plus a `--status` assertion on a non-zero stranded count.
evidence: tracker_maintenance.py:239-241: `regenerable = [p for p in stranded if not path_is_foreign_to_branch(...)]` / `discard_unmerged_paths(tracker, regenerable, stranded_foreign)`
Module docstring: incident was the index left with `unmerged entries and no MERGE_HEAD` — the state this door repairs
Fixture at test file lines 36-57 only creates `src/leak.py` foreign pollution; no test creates an unmerged/conflicted index entry
`test_status_reports_without_writing` (line 72) asserts only `foreign top-level paths : 1`; no assertion on a non-zero `stranded index entries` count or on post-repair stranded-path state
No test in the file invokes the command against a missing tracker dir
advisory.finding: No test exercises the stranded (unmerged-index) repair path, which the command documents as its primary purpose. All tests pollute only with a foreign `src/` tree; none creates an unmerged index entry, so the `_stranded_paths` -> regenerable/stranded_foreign split -> `discard_unmerged_paths` wiring is never verified against real behavior. A regression in that wiring (wrong diff-filter, mis-split of regenerable vs foreign, dropped checkout-from-HEAD) would pass the whole suite.
merged_from: The fatal `rc==2` path when the tracker directory does not exist is untested; exit-codes.md documents `no tracker -> 2` as a contract.
scenarios: A change to `_stranded_paths`'s `--diff-filter=U` or to the regenerable/foreign classification silently breaks the repair with green tests
A regenerable stranded path is deleted instead of restored from HEAD, losing recoverable ticket content, undetected
advisory.suggested_fix: In the fixture or a new test, produce a real unmerged index (e.g. conflicting commits merged with `git merge` leaving `--diff-filter=U` entries), run `--clean`, then assert the index is clean, a regenerable ticket file is restored from HEAD, and the audit line's `stranded_paths` matches.

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 446 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug 2fa6-e3cb-a11f-4e3d has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix this large is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan 2fa6-e3cb-a11f-4e3d` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review 2fa6-e3cb-a11f-4e3d` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan 2fa6-e3cb-a11f-4e3d --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Dispatch tracker-maintenance with init_only=True (or bypass ensure_fresh) so no reconverge/reset runs before the command's own backup-ref + refusal envelope.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:190-195: 'fetch + reconverge … (HEAD-based local-ahead detection, merge-as-union, lock-guarded reset)'

The dispatch comment at src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:342-344 claims it 'must never auto-init' yet init_only=False also triggers a full reconverge that can write/reset the store before the maintenance envelope engages.
dropped.finding: The dispatch arm calls ensure_initialized(init_only=False), which runs reads.ensure_fresh — a throttled fetch + merge-as-union + lock-guarded reset reconverge of the tracker — BEFORE tracker_maintenance_cli takes its backup ref or evaluates its refusal. On the wedged store this command exists to repair, that reconverge can mutate/reset local HEAD, so the backup ref captured later no longer names the pre-maintenance state the operator was shown, undermining the central 'a refused/pre-write run makes NO writes' and 'backup ref before the first write' invariants.
dropped.suggested_fix: Use ensure_initialized(init_only=True) for the tracker-maintenance arm (or resolve the tracker without ensure_fresh), so the command's backup ref and refusal are the first store interaction.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Split git --name-only output on newlines (splitlines()) rather than whitespace so paths with spaces are preserved.
evidence: split() with no argument splits on any whitespace, so a path like `my dir/x.json` becomes `['my','dir/x.json']`.
dropped.finding: _stranded_paths splits `git diff --name-only` output with str.split() (whitespace), so any stranded path containing a space is broken into multiple bogus entries. Those fragments then flow into path_is_foreign_to_branch and discard_unmerged_paths, mis-classifying and mishandling the real paths.
dropped.suggested_fix: return sorted({ln for ln in res.stdout.splitlines() if ln.strip()})
